name: writing a conformance plan
from: Conformance as labels: claims naming bodies instead of designations and editions, ambitions indistinguishable from achievements, and every new document re-inventing its own conformance matrix by hand.
to: The standards program as one ladder: per family, the honest claim today — including 'nothing' — the named target, the gap, a path whose first step an office could take this quarter, and every category-mismatch warning stated plainly; the plan itself asserting no conformance, and auditable at every rung.
cost: The embarrassment of writing 'nothing' in the honest-claim column, family after family, and keeping it there until the evidence exists — the ladder's credibility is bought entirely by its worst rungs.
otherwise: The firm's relationship to public standards stays a mood: labels accrete, category errors ship in prose, stalled ambitions pose as plans, and the day an auditor asks, the answer is archaeology.
